one_liner: VFX-industry image I/O and processing library; its oiiotool ran a crop, resize and convolve job 1.3x faster than ImageMagick 7.
what_it_does: Reads and writes dozens of formats (TIFF, OpenEXR, DPX, Cineon, JPEG, PNG, camera RAW, HEIF, JPEG XL and more) through one format-agnostic ImageInput/ImageOutput plugin API, and holds images in memory as ImageBuf objects that the ImageBufAlgo library operates on (resize, resample, convolve, colour conversion through OpenColorIO, compositing). ImageCache and TextureSystem give bounded-memory access to very large image sets and filtered MIP-map texture lookups for renderers. The oiiotool command line and the Python bindings expose the same operations. It is not a drop-in for ImageMagick: the CLI syntax and the C++ API (free ImageBufAlgo functions with ROI and nthreads arguments) are entirely different.
how_it_is_fast: The measured path has no special algorithm. Every ImageBufAlgo call is split by parallel_image across all cores by default, and oiiotool converts 8-bit input to float once at read time. In 2.5.18, and unchanged on main, IBA::resize evaluates the triangle filter as a direct 2D gather of xtaps x ytaps source pixels per output pixel (5x5 at 90%), with separable tap weights precomputed per column and per row, and IBA::convolve is a plain 3x3 gather; both are scalar loops over ImageBuf iterators. Google Highway SIMD exists in 3.2 only for resample (nearest/bilinear) and some per-pixel arithmetic, so the margin over ImageMagick comes from whole-pipeline threading and lower per-operation overhead (inferred from the code, not profiled), not from a faster resampler.
when_to_use: Pipelines built around OpenEXR (multi-part, deep), DPX/Cineon, tiled or MIP-mapped TIFF and OCIO colour management, where you need one C++/Python API across formats more than peak resize speed.
Batch jobs that shell out to ImageMagick convert/magick for crop, resize and convolution of large images on a many-core box: oiiotool 2.5.18 was 1.27x to 1.28x faster in the libvips table.
Applications that must read huge texture or plate sets with bounded memory: ImageCache keeps a capped working set and is documented as fully thread-safe.
Renderers and texture tools needing filtered MIP-map lookups (TextureSystem, maketx / oiiotool -otex).
when_not_to_use: Throughput-first thumbnailing or web resizing: in the same libvips table libvips (0.57 s), GraphicsMagick (2.05 s), FFmpeg (2.06 s) and OpenCV (3.15 s) all beat oiio (3.46 s).
Memory-constrained hosts: oiiotool promotes 8-bit input to float unless --native is given, and peaked at 2236.57 MB against 1500.52 MB for magick and 94.28 MB for libvips.

Strong downscales with IBA::resize: the 2D gather reads (2*ceil(r/scale)+1)^2 source pixels per output pixel, so a 10% shrink costs 441 taps with the triangle filter and 3721 with the default lanczos3, against 42 and 122 for a two-pass separable resampler; use a dedicated resizer there (IBA::resample is cheap but does not filter, so it aliases).

Untrusted input on old or distro builds: SECURITY.md says 2.5.x and earlier get no patches, and the 3.2 changelog lists dozens of reader hardening fixes including CVE-2026-59181 (Cineon), CVE-2026-59156 (FITS), CVE-2026-63422 (OpenEXR out-of-bounds write) and CVE-2026-63420 (PSD).
Projects that want a small dependency: the required set alone is Imath, OpenEXR, libTIFF, OpenColorIO, libjpeg, zlib, fmt and robin-map, plus CMake 3.23.

integration.dependencies: Required: Imath >= 3.1, OpenEXR >= 3.1, libTIFF >= 4.1, OpenColorIO >= 2.3, libjpeg >= 9 or libjpeg-turbo >= 2.1, zlib >= 1.2.7, fmt >= 9 and robin-map >= 1.3 (the last two auto-downloaded if missing). Optional per format or feature: libpng, LibRaw, FFmpeg, OpenJPEG, OpenJPH, libheif, libwebp, libjxl, giflib, DCMTK, OpenVDB, Ptex, Freetype, libultrahdr, TBB, OpenCV, Qt (iv viewer), Python with nanobind or pybind11, Google Highway (OIIO_USE_HWY).
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (also C++20/23/26); gcc 9.3-16, clang 10-22, MSVC 2017-2026 (v19.14+), Intel oneAPI 2022+; CMake >= 3.23 for the 3.2 line
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows; x86-64 builds default to an SSE4.2 baseline in 3.2 (x86-64-v2 on main), with NEON paths on aarch64
integration.thread_safety: ImageCache is documented as completely thread-safe; ImageBufAlgo functions parallelise internally over nthreads (default: all cores; pass 1 if the caller is already multithreaded). 3.2 fixed an ImageBuf data race that could corrupt multithreaded reads (#5325).

gotchas: The libvips oiio.sh bug survives on current main: the script passes '--crop 9800+100+100' (undefined $widthx), and scan_offset on main still parses the leading '9800+100' as an offset and ignores the rest, so a re-run on OIIO 3.2 again processes a mostly black 10000x10000 frame.
oiiotool works in float by default; use --native (or read with the native type in the C++ API) to keep 8-bit data, at your own speed and accuracy trade-off (not benchmarked).

The docs say Highway SIMD is enabled by default, but the OIIO_USE_HWY CMake option is OFF ('experimental'), so check how your build was configured before expecting those speedups; the filtered resize and convolve paths have no Highway code either way.

IBA::resize takes filter options through KWArgs (filtername, filterwidth); with no name it picks lanczos3 when shrinking and blackman-harris when enlarging, and widens the filter by the enlargement ratio, so pin the filter for reproducible output and cost.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick OpenImageIO over libvips, GraphicsMagick or FFmpeg only when you need its VFX format coverage (deep and multi-part EXR, DPX, MIP-mapped textures), OCIO colour management or ImageCache/TextureSystem; for batch resize and convolution throughput libvips was 6x faster and used about 24x less memory in the same table, and fast_image_resize or zimg are better single-kernel resizers.
verified_claims_summary: In the libvips maintainer's vips-bench run (12 Aug 2025, Threadripper PRO 3955WX 16 cores, Ubuntu 25.04 packages, flags not stated), oiiotool 2.5.18 took 3.46 s, best wall time of five, to load a 10000x10000 8-bit tiled TIFF, crop, triangle-resize to 90%, 3x3-convolve and save, against 4.41 s for ImageMagick 7.1.1 magick and 4.44 s for convert, about 1.3x (derived from page data). The oiio script's broken crop made it process a mostly black 10000x10000 frame (about 4% more output pixels than ImageMagick) with a gaussian instead of a sharpen kernel, so the work is comparable but the output is not the intended image.
status_note: Very active Academy Software Foundation project (3.2.1.0 released 1 Oct 2026, commits on 3 Oct 2026, monthly patch releases) under Apache-2.0; the benchmarked 2.5 line no longer gets security fixes, so use 3.2.x.
